Reference-based bootstrap for signature and composition uncertainty

Source: R/03_03_resampling_inference.R
reference_bootstrap_decovart.Rd

The frequentist DeCovarT likelihood treats \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) and each \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\) as known. In a labelled, reference-based model those moments come from purified profiles whose cell-type names stay attached. This bootstrap resamples the experimental units that generated the reference (donors, by default), re-estimates the plug-in moments and refits (Efron 1979) .

Usage

reference_bootstrap_decovart(
  y,
  reference_profiles,
  donor_ids = NULL,
  method = c("donors", "cells"),
  n_boot = 199L,
  level = 0.95,
  regenerate_bulk = FALSE,
  p = NULL,
  n_replicates = NULL,
  ridge = 1e-06,
  epsilon = 10^-8,
  itmax = 500L
)

Arguments

y

Numeric vector of length \(G\), or \(G\times N\) matrix of replicate bulk profiles that share one composition; their log-likelihoods are summed (the pooled, population-level fit).

reference_profiles

Named list of \(G\times n_j\) matrices, one purified sample matrix per cell type (at least two columns each). The list order fixes the column order of the signature.

donor_ids

Donor (or other clustering) labels: a list named like reference_profiles, with one label per purified column. Required for method = "donors".

method

One of "donors" (default) or "cells".

n_boot

Number of bootstrap replicates.

level

Confidence level for percentile intervals.

regenerate_bulk

If TRUE, simulate a new bulk from the fitted model and refit it with the bootstrapped moments, instead of keeping the observed \(\boldsymbol{Y}\) fixed.

p

Composition to simulate from. Defaults to the MLE computed from y (or the restricted MLE under null_value).

n_replicates

Number of bulk columns simulated per replicate; defaults to the number of observed columns.

ridge

Non-negative ridge multiple for the sample covariance of each cell type. The default 1e-6 is relative to the mean diagonal.

epsilon, itmax

Relative convergence tolerance and iteration budget passed to stats::nlminb().

Value

A list with method, estimates (\(J\times\) n_boot), interval (percentile bounds), n_failed, mean_signature_matrix / Sigma from the original reference, and p_hat from the original plug-in fit.

Details

Permuting gene order, or permuting cell-type labels of an already averaged signature, is not a bootstrap: the first destroys the gene-wise pairing of bulk and reference, and the second is algebraic equivariance rather than a source of uncertainty (see equivariance_check_decovart() and vignette("theory-DeCovarT-MLE-properties")). The two method options instead resample, with replacement, units that actually vary.

donors

Cluster bootstrap: resample donor identifiers within each cell type, take every purified column of the sampled donors (a donor drawn twice is included twice), rebuild \((\boldsymbol{\mu},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\), and refit. This is the default: it targets biological / reference-population uncertainty rather than technical cell-level noise alone.

cells

Resample purified columns independently within each cell type (with replacement) and rebuild the plug-in moments. Use this when donor labels are unavailable.

The observed bulk is kept fixed unless regenerate_bulk = TRUE, in which case each replicate also draws \(\boldsymbol{Y}^{(b)}\) from the fitted model, at p (the observed MLE by default) and the moments of the full reference, and refits it with the bootstrapped moments \(S^{(b)}\). Drawing \(\boldsymbol{Y}^{(b)}\) from \(S^{(b)}\) instead would make each refit consistent with its own moments, so the reference error would not reach \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}^{(b)}\): with 60 cells per type, that variant covered a known composition 76\ level, against 92\

When a cell type has fewer purified columns than genes, the sample covariance is singular. A ridge ridge * mean(diag(S)) is then added on the diagonal so that \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) remains factorisable. Set ridge = 0 to disable that guard (and accept possible Cholesky failures).

References

Efron B (1979). “Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife.” The Annals of Statistics, 7(1), 1–26. doi:10.1214/aos/1176344552 .

Examples

set.seed(1)
mu <- matrix(c(20, 40, 15, 40, 20, 25), nrow = 3)
colnames(mu) <- paste0("ct", 1:2)
Sigma <- array(c(diag(3), diag(3)), dim = c(3, 3, 2))
refs <- lapply(seq_len(2), function(j) {
  t(MASS::mvrnorm(n = 8, mu = mu[, j], Sigma = Sigma[, , j]))
})
names(refs) <- colnames(mu)
donor_ids <- lapply(refs, function(x) {
  rep(paste0("d", 1:2), length.out = ncol(x))
})
y <- drop(mu %*% c(0.6, 0.4))
reference_bootstrap_decovart(
  y,
  refs,
  donor_ids = donor_ids,
  n_boot = 15
)$interval
#>          2.5%     97.5%
#> ct1 0.6016025 0.6234908
#> ct2 0.3765092 0.3983975
